summary: Hampshire County tower on Nathaniel Mountain, built in 1939 and staffed each spring and fall into the late 1970s; climbing is not permitted and a 2021 visit reported broken glass.

facts.design: four-legged steel structure with a glass-enclosed cab

access.note: The hike to the tower is on the public Nathaniel Mountain Wildlife Management Area. Climbing the tower is not permitted.

visit.trail_note: About 4.5-mile round trip from the base of Mill Run Road

events.note: Reported as built in 1939 by DC News Now and ICPRB; the register says only that it was built before 1941
1941 National Geodetic Survey station description: a 4-legged steel structure about 90 feet high with a glass-enclosed cab
1948 U.S. Geological Survey recovery note: the station was recovered in good condition and the tower's name was now Hampshire Tower
Visit report September 12, 2021: first flight of stairs removed; a lot of glass broken out

notes_for_editor: Built year is consistent: 1939 in DC News Now and ICPRB, and the register says prior to 1941. The 1941 federal station description and the 1948 recovery note (name now Hampshire Tower) come from a single Forest Lookouts page that quotes the NGS record; the rename rests on that one note, and a search snippet claiming the same rename was not used. The DC News Now article is undated in the cache, so the late-1970s staffing and the 'oak steps missing' description are not dated precisely. The most recent condition evidence is the NHLR visit report of September 2021, which is not an access or status check. Access: the public WMA hike is roughly 4.5 miles round trip, and climbing is not permitted (ICPRB). The story does not describe any climb. Suggest considering 'Hampshire Tower' as an alternate name for other_names; this is not a correction. Status 'standing' is supported by the FFLA listing and the register. Photos: the record already has the NHLR 2016 and 2021 photos; no new ones added. Page-read budget: the two FFLA list pages and e-WV were read as shared context, so this tower used six distinct pages plus one WebSearch.
